metadata.title: Electronic Submission Template for Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) Applications: Draft Guidance for Sponsors and Food and Drug Administration Staff
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.
metadata.applicability: Products: Biologics, Medical Devices. Topics: Electronic Submissions

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: In section 745A(b)(3) of the FD&C Act, Congress granted explicit statutory authorization to 40 FDA to specify in guidance the electronic submissions requirement by providing standards, 41 criteria for waivers and exemptions, and a timetable for such electronic submission standards. 42 Accordingly, to the extent that this document provides such requirements under section 43 745A(b)(3) of the FD&C Act, indicated by the use of mandatory words, such as must or 44 required, this draft guidance is not subject to the usual restrictions in section 701(h) of the FD&C 45 Act and FDA’s good guidance practices (GGPs) regulations, such as the requirement that 46 guidances not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. See 21 CFR 10.115(d). 47
candidates.context: FDA’s guidance document “ Providing Regulatory Submissions for Medical Devices in 30 Electronic Format — Submissions Under Section 745A(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and 31 Cosmetic Act ” (hereafter referred to as the “745A(b) device parent guidance”) provides a 32 process for the development of templates to facilitate the preparation, submission, and review of 33 regulatory submissions for medical devices solely in electronic format. As described in the 34 745A(b) device parent guidance, FDA plans to implement the requirements of section 35 745A(b)(3) of the FD&C Act with individual guidances specifying the formats for specific 36 submissions and corresponding timetables for implementation. candidates.statement: Information Requested Description Report of Prior Investigations A complete report of prior investigations of the device under 21 CFR 812.20(b). This must include reports of all prior non-clinical and clinical testing of the device required under 21 CFR 812.27.
candidates.context: 22 As discussed in the guidance titled “ Factors to Consider When Making Benefit-Risk Determinations for Medical Device Investigational Device Exemptions ,” FDA’s assessment of benefits and risks for an IDE application takes into account the contextual setting in which the study is being proposed, including but not limited to characterization of disease or condition being treated or diagnosed, and the availability of and risks associated with alternative treatments or diagnostics. Reprocessing Information for assessing the reprocessing validation and labeling, if applicable ( see FDA guidance “ Reprocessing Medical Devices in Health Care Settings: Validation Methods and Labeling ”).

candidates.statement: Waivers 205 At this time, FDA has not identified any particular circumstances appropriate for a waiver of the 206 IDE electronic submission requirements and does not intend to grant requests for waiver. Given 207 the widespread availability of software to enable use of the current IDE eSTAR PDF (available 208 to download on FDA’s website), all sponsors should have the ability to provide an IDE 209 eSTAR. 29
candidates.context: Please note that IDE submissions related to expanded access compassionate use requests and 197 reports and emergency use reports, 28 and adverse event reports (all types, e.g., serious, 198 malfunctions) are already exempt from submission solely in electronic format, as stated in the 199 FDA guidance “ Providing Regulatory Submissions for Medical Devices in Electronic Format - 200 Submissions Under Section 745A(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act .” Although 201 submission in electronic format will not be required for these submission types, FDA encourages 202 submission in available electronic formats of these submissions to facilitate the review process. 203 B. candidates.statement: As described in the 745A(b) device parent guidance, this draft guidance, once finalized, will be 213 used to specify the corresponding timetable(s) for implementation of IDE electronic submissions. 214 FDA intends to provide a transition period of a minimum of one year from the final guidance 215 issuance prior to requiring that IDE applications be provided as electronic submissions. 216 Currently, and during the transition period, eSTARs may be used voluntarily for IDE electronic 217 submissions. As instructed at the website for the eSTAR Program (under the heading, “How to 218 prepare a submission using eSTAR” 30 ), the electronic submission must be submitted using 219 FDA’s electronic portal when submitting to CDRH.
